findings.title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper has no effect — parent is not a flex container
findings.body: The diff adds `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The `order` property only applies to flex/grid children, but the natural parent in this file, `.title-wrapper` (lines 3–16), is still `float: left; width: 90%;` and was not converted to a flex container in this PR. Therefore the `order` declaration is dead CSS and does nothing at runtime. If the intent was to reorder the topic header elements via flex, the wrapping container (likely `.title-wrapper` or a parent in another stylesheet) must also be set to `@include flexbox();` for `order` to take effect.

findings.title: Children of the new flex container .contents still rely on float: left
findings.body: `.contents` is converted to a flex container via `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`, but its descendants still use `float: left` to lay out horizontally: `.icons` (line 54), `.icons > li` (line 60), and `.login-button, button.sign-up-button` (line 43). In a flex container, `float` is ignored by the layout engine, so these declarations become dead code and the visual arrangement may not match the developer's expectation. The floats should be removed (and `.icons > li` re-laid out via flex properties such as `display: flex`) so the layout actually flows as flex intends.

findings.title: Avatar floats inside the new flex container .small-action are silently dropped
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), but its descendants `.topic-avatar` (line 270, `float: left;`) and `.avatar` inside `.small-action-desc` (line 298, `float: left;`) still rely on floats for horizontal positioning. In a flex container `float` is ignored, so the original float-based layout around the avatars may silently change. The avatar positioning intent should be re-expressed with flex properties (e.g. `flex: 0 0 auto; margin-right`) rather than left as `float`, and the now-obsolete `float: left` declarations removed.

findings.title: Removing margin-top: 5px on .badge-wrapper.bullet may misalign the bullet badge
findings.body: The diff removes `.badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` (originally compensating for the surrounding line-height) and at the same time adds `line-height: 1.5;` to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The bullet badge previously relied on that 5px top offset to sit on the text baseline; with the offset removed and a larger line-height, the bullet may now sit visually misaligned within `.extra-info-wrapper` unless another mechanism (e.g. flex `align-items` on the new flex parent, once that exists) restores the alignment.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits the non-standard `-ms-align-items` property
findings.body: The new `@mixin align-items` emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;` on line 121. `-ms-align-items` is not a recognized CSS property — the real Microsoft/IE10 alias is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on the preceding line 120). The `-ms-align-items` declaration is dead code that no browser honors and should be removed to avoid confusion. Line 120 also has trailing whitespace after `$alignment;` before the semicolon, which is harmless but should be cleaned up.

findings.title: PR description is just "Test 5" — does not describe the change
findings.body: The pull request description reads only "Test 5", which conveys nothing about intent (layout rework, perf experiment, bug fix, etc.) or scope (the diff touches header, topic, topic-post and badges SCSS plus new flexbox mixins). Maintainers and reviewers have to infer the purpose from the diff. A meaningful description (e.g. "Replace float-based header/small-action layout with flexbox via new mixins in mixins.scss") should be provided before merging.
